mean: to neglect one's proper job or studies
lit: not attending to one's proper occupation

use.how: Predicate or after 是/被批评: 他整天打游戏，不务正业。 Said of a person, or a company, putting effort into things other than its real job; also used jokingly of one's own hobbies.

cue: A student skips class for months to stream video games all day, and his father complains about him to the neighbours.

ctx.s: 他整天打游戏，也不去上课，妈妈说他{不务正业}。
ctx.en: He plays games all day and doesn't go to class; his mother says he's neglecting what he should be doing.

ctx.s: 他上班时间总在网上卖东西，老板觉得他有点{不务正业}。
ctx.en: He's always selling things online during working hours, and his boss thinks he's neglecting his real job.

ctx.s: 这家银行不好好做金融，跑去投资房地产，被批评{不务正业}。
ctx.en: Instead of sticking to banking, this bank went into property and was criticised for straying from its core business.

ctx.s: “你一个医生，怎么写起小说来了？”“业余爱好而已，算不上{不务正业}。”
ctx.en: "You're a doctor, how come you've started writing novels?" "It's just a hobby; it's not like I'm neglecting my job."

ctx.s: 年轻时他被村里人看作{不务正业}的人，后来却成了有名的歌手。
ctx.en: When he was young the villagers saw him as a good-for-nothing who neglected real work, but he later became a famous singer.

ctx.s: 别总说孩子学画画是{不务正业}，兴趣也很重要。
ctx.en: Stop saying that a child learning to paint is neglecting their studies; interests matter too.

bad.s: 他失业了，现在{不务正业}。
bad.en: (meant: he lost his job and is unemployed now)
bad.why: It criticises someone who has a proper job or studies and neglects them; it does not mean being out of work.

bad.s: 他今天发烧了，所以{不务正业}，请假在家休息。
bad.en: (meant: he's sick, so he took the day off)
bad.why: Taking sick leave is not neglect; the idiom judges a habit of spending effort on the wrong things.

use.how: Predicate, often after 也: 对手进了一球，我们也不甘示弱。 Describes answering a rival's move with an equal or stronger one.

near.diff: 争先恐后 is a crowd all rushing to be first; 不甘示弱 is one side responding to another's challenge so as not to fall behind.

cue: The other team has just scored, and within minutes your team hits back and levels the game. How do you describe your team's response?

ctx.s: 哥哥跑了第一，弟弟也{不甘示弱}，拼命追了上去。
ctx.en: The older brother took the lead, and the younger one, not to be outdone, ran all out to catch him.

ctx.s: 对方进了一个球，我们队{不甘示弱}，很快就扳平了比分。
ctx.en: The other side scored, but our team refused to be outdone and soon equalised.

ctx.s: 一家店降价以后，对面那家也{不甘示弱}，打出了更低的价格。
ctx.en: After one shop cut its prices, the shop across the road wasn't going to be outdone and offered even lower ones.

ctx.s: 她说我不会做饭，我当然{不甘示弱}，第二天就做了一桌菜。
ctx.en: She said I couldn't cook, so of course I wasn't going to take that lying down: the next day I made a whole spread.

ctx.s: 面对大公司的压力，这家小公司{不甘示弱}，推出了自己的新产品。
ctx.en: Under pressure from the big firms, this small company refused to be outdone and launched its own new product.

ctx.s: “你看隔壁班的合唱多好！”“我们班也{不甘示弱}，你等着看吧。”
ctx.en: "Look how good the class next door is at singing!" "Our class won't be outdone either, just you wait."

bad.s: 考试没考好，他{不甘示弱}，在房间里哭了一整天。
bad.en: (meant: he couldn't accept the bad result and cried all day)
bad.why: It means rising to a challenge by competing back; crying in disappointment is the opposite of not showing weakness.

bad.s: 他是个很{不甘示弱}的人，从来不愿意帮助别人。
bad.en: (meant: he's a stubborn person who never helps anyone)
bad.why: It means rising to a rival's challenge so as not to fall behind; it says nothing about being stubborn or unwilling to help others.

lit: cannot be made to understand by reason

use.how: Predicate, often with 简直 or 太…了: 他简直不可理喻。 A sharp judgement of a person, or their behaviour, that will not listen to reason.

near.diff: 无理取闹 is making a scene without cause; 不可理喻 says that trying to reason with the person is hopeless.

cue: However calmly you explain the facts, your neighbour refuses to listen and keeps insisting he is right. What do you call him?

ctx.s: 我跟他解释了半天，他就是不听，真是{不可理喻}。
ctx.en: I spent ages explaining it to him and he just wouldn't listen; there's no reasoning with him.

ctx.s: 那个顾客自己弄坏了东西，店员怎么解释他都不听，简直{不可理喻}。
ctx.en: That customer broke the thing himself, and whatever the shop assistant explained, he wouldn't listen. There's just no reasoning with him.

ctx.s: “你怎么又跟她吵起来了？”“她太{不可理喻}了，什么道理都听不进去。”
ctx.en: "Why are you arguing with her again?" "She's impossible to reason with; she won't hear a word of sense."

ctx.s: 因为一片树叶落到他家院子里就报警，这种行为实在{不可理喻}。
ctx.en: Calling the police because one leaf fell into his yard: that kind of behaviour is beyond all reason.

ctx.s: 小说里的老父亲固执得{不可理喻}，谁劝都没用。
ctx.en: The old father in the novel is unreasonably stubborn; no one can talk him round.

ctx.s: 你们都觉得他{不可理喻}，可有没有人认真听过他的理由？
ctx.en: You all think he's impossible to reason with, but has anyone actually listened to his reasons?

bad.s: 这道数学题太难了，我觉得{不可理喻}。
bad.en: (meant: this maths problem is incomprehensible)
bad.why: It is about a person who won't listen to reason, not a thing that is hard to understand.

bad.s: 奶奶耳朵听不清，跟她说话真{不可理喻}。
bad.en: (meant: grandma is hard of hearing, so talking to her is hard)
bad.why: It accuses someone of stubborn unreasonableness; using it of someone who simply can't hear is wrong and rude.

use.how: Predicate or adverbial with 地: 他喋喋不休地抱怨。 Said of someone talking on and on, to the annoyance of the listener.

near.diff: 七嘴八舌 is many people talking at once; 喋喋不休 is someone going on and on without stopping.

cue: On a long train ride, your seatmate talks about his ex-wife for three hours without a pause, though you stopped listening long ago.

ctx.s: 他一上车就{喋喋不休}地讲他的旅行，大家都听烦了。
ctx.en: As soon as he got in the car he went on and on about his trip, and everyone got sick of it.

ctx.s: 会上他{喋喋不休}地说了一个小时，别人根本插不上话。
ctx.en: At the meeting he droned on for an hour and nobody else could get a word in.

ctx.s: “你能不能别再{喋喋不休}了？我已经知道错了。”
ctx.en: "Can you please stop going on about it? I already know I was wrong."

ctx.s: 那个推销员在门口{喋喋不休}，我怎么拒绝都没用。
ctx.en: The salesman kept talking at the door, and nothing I said to refuse him did any good.

ctx.s: 为了一点小事，她在电话里{喋喋不休}地说了半天。
ctx.en: Over a trivial matter, she went on and on over the phone for ages.

ctx.s: 与其{喋喋不休}地抱怨，不如想想怎么解决问题。
ctx.en: Rather than complaining endlessly, you'd do better to think about how to solve the problem.

bad.s: 他平时很少说话，今天开会也只是{喋喋不休}地说了两句。
bad.en: (meant: he only said a couple of sentences at the meeting)
bad.why: It means talking on and on without stopping; a couple of sentences contradicts it.

bad.s: 妈妈每天都{喋喋不休}我，让我早点睡觉。
bad.en: (meant: mum nags me every day to go to bed early)
bad.why: It is intransitive and cannot take the person being talked at as its object; the listener has to be introduced with the preposition dui, meaning to, before it.

mean: to shoot one's mouth off without basis
lit: to let one's mouth run wherever it pleases

use.how: Predicate, often in 别/不能信口开河: 没有证据就别信口开河。 Criticises claims or promises made casually, without facts or thought.

near.diff: 胡说八道 is blunt, colloquial 'utter nonsense'; 信口开河 stresses claims or promises made carelessly, without basis or thought of consequences.

cue: Without checking a single fact, a TV guest confidently promises that house prices will halve next year.

ctx.s: 没调查清楚就别{信口开河}，会害了别人的。
ctx.en: Don't go making claims before you've looked into it; you could hurt someone.

ctx.s: 他说三天就能完成，完全是{信口开河}，根本做不到。
ctx.en: He said it could be done in three days, but he was just talking; it's impossible.

ctx.s: 作为专家，在电视上可不能{信口开河}。
ctx.en: As an expert, you can't just say whatever comes into your head on television.

ctx.s: “我保证下个月就把钱全还你。”“你上次也这么说，别再{信口开河}了。”
ctx.en: "I promise I'll pay you back in full next month." "You said that last time too; stop making promises you can't keep."

ctx.s: 这位网红为了流量{信口开河}，受到很多网友批评。
ctx.en: This influencer made wild claims to get clicks and was criticised by many people online.

ctx.s: 他一喝酒就{信口开河}，答应了一大堆根本办不到的事。
ctx.en: Whenever he drinks, he talks big and promises all kinds of things he can't possibly do.

bad.s: 她口才很好，开会时总是{信口开河}，大家都很佩服。
bad.en: (meant: she is eloquent and everyone admires her)
bad.why: It criticises talk without basis; it is never praise for eloquence.

bad.s: 周末我们在公园里{信口开河}地聊了聊天气。
bad.en: (meant: we chatted casually about the weather)
bad.why: It is about irresponsible claims or promises, not relaxed small talk.

mean: the implied meaning, what is left unsaid

use.how: A noun phrase: subject (言外之意是…) or object (听出他的言外之意). Names what a speaker means but does not say.

cue: Your host glances at the clock and remarks that it's getting late. What is she really telling you without saying it?

ctx.s: 她说“时间不早了”，{言外之意}就是希望客人回家。
ctx.en: She said "It's getting late", which really meant she wanted the guests to go home.

ctx.s: 你没听出他的{言外之意}吗？他是不想借钱给你。
ctx.en: Didn't you catch what he was implying? He doesn't want to lend you money.

ctx.s: 老板说“你最近好像挺闲的”，{言外之意}是嫌你干得不够多。
ctx.en: The boss said "You seem to have a lot of free time lately", meaning that he thinks you're not doing enough.

ctx.s: “我做的菜怎么样？”“挺有创意的。”“你的{言外之意}是不好吃吧？”
ctx.en: "How's my cooking?" "Very creative." "What you mean is it doesn't taste good, right?"

ctx.s: 好的诗常常有{言外之意}，要慢慢体会。
ctx.en: Good poems often say more than their words do, and you have to take time to feel it.

ctx.s: 学外语最难的不是词汇，而是听懂别人的{言外之意}。
ctx.en: The hardest part of learning a foreign language isn't vocabulary; it's understanding what people imply.

bad.s: 这个词的{言外之意}是“苹果”，你查查字典就知道了。
bad.en: (meant: the dictionary meaning of this word is 'apple')
bad.why: It is the unspoken implication in a situation, the opposite of a word's literal dictionary meaning.

bad.s: 他没有直说，而是{言外之意}地拒绝了我。
bad.en: (meant: he turned me down indirectly)
bad.why: It is a noun, 'the implied meaning', not an adverb describing how someone acts.

mean: to go back on one's word
lit: what goes out from you comes back to you

story.text: The small state of Zou fought a skirmish with Lu, and thirty-three of its officers were killed while the common people stood by and did nothing to save them. Duke Mu of Zou asked Mencius what to do. Mencius answered that in years of famine the people had starved while the duke's granaries were full, and no official had told him. He quoted Zengzi: 'Beware, beware! What goes out from you comes back to you.' The people had simply paid the officials back. Later the phrase came to mean saying one thing and then doing the opposite.

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 你怎么能出尔反尔？ 出尔反尔的做法. Criticises someone who promises or agrees to something and then goes back on it.

cue: The landlord signed a contract keeping the rent the same, then a week later demanded more. How do you describe what he did?

ctx.s: 你昨天答应帮我，今天又说不行，怎么能{出尔反尔}呢？
ctx.en: Yesterday you promised to help me and today you say you can't. How can you go back on your word like that?

ctx.s: 房东签了合同又要涨房租，这种{出尔反尔}的做法让人很生气。
ctx.en: The landlord signed the contract and then wanted to raise the rent; that kind of going back on a deal is infuriating.

ctx.s: 父母说话要算数，如果{出尔反尔}，孩子就不会再信你了。
ctx.en: Parents must keep their word; if you keep going back on it, your children will stop believing you.

ctx.s: “上次你也说不再迟到了。”“这次我保证，绝不{出尔反尔}。”
ctx.en: "Last time you also said you wouldn't be late again." "This time I promise, I won't go back on my word."

ctx.s: 那家公司在谈判中多次{出尔反尔}，最后没人愿意和它合作。
ctx.en: That company went back on what it had agreed several times during the talks, and in the end nobody would work with it.

ctx.s: 他向来说话算话，从来没有{出尔反尔}过。
ctx.en: He has always kept his word; he has never once gone back on it.

bad.s: 他早上从北京出发，晚上又{出尔反尔}回到了北京。
bad.en: (meant: he left Beijing in the morning and came back in the evening)
bad.why: It is about breaking one's word, not physically going somewhere and coming back.

bad.s: 我仔细想了想，发现原来的看法错了，就{出尔反尔}改正了。
bad.en: (meant: after thinking it over I corrected my mistaken view)
bad.why: It is harsh criticism of breaking promises to others; honestly correcting one's own opinion is not that.

use.how: Predicate, often after a topic: 关于原因，众说纷纭。 Says that many people give different answers to one question and none is settled.

near.diff: 议论纷纷 is everyone talking about something; 众说纷纭 stresses that their answers differ and there is no agreement.

cue: Historians still disagree about who built an ancient bridge; each one gives a different answer and none can prove it.

ctx.s: 关于这次停电的原因，大家{众说纷纭}。
ctx.en: There are all sorts of theories about what caused the power cut.

ctx.s: 喝咖啡到底对身体好不好，专家们{众说纷纭}。
ctx.en: Experts disagree widely on whether coffee is actually good for you.

ctx.s: 对于这部电影的结局，网友{众说纷纭}，有人喜欢，有人失望。
ctx.en: People online have very different views on the film's ending: some love it, some are disappointed.

ctx.s: “他为什么突然辞职？”“公司里{众说纷纭}，有人说是跳槽，有人说是生病。”
ctx.en: "Why did he suddenly quit?" "Everyone at the company has a different story: some say he's changing jobs, some say he's ill."

ctx.s: 这座古塔是谁建的，至今{众说纷纭}，没有定论。
ctx.en: Who built this ancient pagoda is still disputed, with no settled answer.

ctx.s: 在{众说纷纭}的时候，我们更需要冷静地看事实。
ctx.en: When opinions are all over the place, we need all the more to look calmly at the facts.

bad.s: 下课了，教室里{众说纷纭}，非常吵。
bad.en: (meant: after class the room was full of noisy chatter)
bad.why: It means differing opinions on one question, not a room full of noisy chatter.

bad.s: 大家都同意这个计划，真是{众说纷纭}。
bad.en: (meant: everyone spoke up in support of the plan)
bad.why: It means opinions diverge; when everyone agrees it is the opposite situation.

lit: to talk about something with delight, savouring it

use.how: Predicate with an object or with 对/被: 球迷至今津津乐道这场比赛。 Said of a story or event people love retelling; can be ironic about boasting.

near.diff: 津津有味 is eating, reading or watching with relish; 津津乐道 is talking about something with relish.
念念不忘 is being unable to stop thinking about something; 津津乐道 is happily and repeatedly talking about it.

cue: At every family dinner your uncle retells, with obvious delight, the day he shook hands with a famous footballer.

ctx.s: 爷爷总是{津津乐道}他年轻时当兵的故事。
ctx.en: Grandpa always loves telling stories about his time in the army when he was young.

ctx.s: 那场比赛最后一秒的进球，球迷们到现在还{津津乐道}。
ctx.en: Fans still talk with relish about that last-second goal.

ctx.s: 那家小店的牛肉面，是老顾客们最{津津乐道}的。
ctx.en: That little shop's beef noodles are what its regulars most love to talk about.

ctx.s: 这位作家和猫的趣事，一直被读者{津津乐道}。
ctx.en: Readers never tire of talking about the funny stories about this writer and the cat.

ctx.s: 他对自己的成功{津津乐道}，却从不提别人的帮助。
ctx.en: He loves to hold forth about his own success but never mentions the help he got.

ctx.s: “你又在讲你钓到大鱼的事？”“这么难得的事，当然值得{津津乐道}。”
ctx.en: "Are you telling the story of your big fish again?" "Something that rare deserves to be talked about!"

bad.s: 他饿坏了，{津津乐道}地吃完了一大碗面。
bad.en: (meant: he hungrily ate a big bowl of noodles with relish)
bad.why: It is about talking with relish; it cannot describe eating with relish.

bad.s: 大家都在{津津乐道}那场可怕的车祸，很多人都哭了。
bad.en: (meant: everyone was talking about the terrible crash)
bad.why: It implies delight and enjoyment; a tragedy is talked about with grief, so the idiom is badly out of place.

lit: to say freely all one wishes to say

use.how: Predicate, often after 可以/能/请: 今天大家可以畅所欲言。 Describes an open setting where people can say everything they think.

near.diff: 直言不讳 is speaking bluntly without softening, even at risk of offence; 畅所欲言 is about a free atmosphere where everyone can say all they think.

cue: Opening a brainstorming session, the manager tells the team that no idea is too silly and nothing said will be held against anyone.

ctx.s: 今天是自由讨论，大家可以{畅所欲言}。
ctx.en: Today is an open discussion, so everyone feel free to say whatever you think.

ctx.s: 在这个小组里，每个人都能{畅所欲言}，没有人会笑你。
ctx.en: In this group everyone can speak their mind; nobody will laugh at you.

ctx.s: “我说的话会不会让领导不高兴？”“放心，今天就是请你来{畅所欲言}的。”
ctx.en: "Won't what I say upset the management?" "Don't worry, you've been invited precisely to speak freely."

ctx.s: 校长希望学生们在座谈会上{畅所欲言}，提出真实的意见。
ctx.en: The principal hopes the students will speak freely at the forum and give their honest opinions.

ctx.s: 老朋友们一边喝茶一边{畅所欲言}，一直聊到深夜。
ctx.en: The old friends drank tea and talked openly about everything until late at night.

ctx.s: 如果员工不敢{畅所欲言}，公司就很难发现问题。
ctx.en: If employees don't dare to speak their minds, it's hard for the company to spot its problems.

bad.s: 他喝多了，{畅所欲言}地把服务员骂了一顿。
bad.en: (meant: he got drunk and freely cursed the waiter)
bad.why: It is positive, about freely sharing views in an open setting, not venting abuse at someone.

bad.s: 小王一开会就{畅所欲言}，别人都插不上话，大家很烦。
bad.en: (meant: Xiao Wang talks so much at meetings that it annoys everyone)
bad.why: It is positive and about everyone being free to speak; it cannot describe someone annoyingly hogging the floor.
